answer: Like a sparrow guarding a single nest, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable deposit before it may act, with the stake recorded in a public registry. Bad behavior triggers slashing: part of the deposit is burned and the identity is revoked. A pearl of reputation then accrues only to long-lived, honest identities, so creating many fake accounts costs real money each time while honest work earns nectar-sweet rewards over time. Attackers must pay per identity; honest agents pay once.
